text:
Artyom Levshunov is getting the minutes a No. 2 overall pick gets, more than 20 a night, and he reached 100 NHL games on Oct. 31 (per Blackhawk Up). The results are tough. He has 3 points in 18 games and none in his last ten, and with him at five on five the Blackhawks get 38% of the expected goals (the share of chance quality), worse than the team does without him.

Some of that is luck: Chicago has scored 4.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey noted he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league last season. But the defense is the real concern. Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more chances with him out there than with almost any other defenseman (bottom 1%).

Patience is the honest read. Of the defensemen picked in the top four since 2005 with four-plus seasons, 16 of 17 reached 200 NHL games, and Victor Hedman scored 0.27 points a game in his first full season. The tools are there, with speed bursts in the 85th percentile and a hard shot. We'd watch his reads in his own end more than his point total.
headline: Artyom Levshunov's hard lessons
